independent_reasoning: Independence bookkeeping: alpha(A-S)<=alpha(A)=4 by heredity from I5-freeness, with alpha(A)=4 from R(4,4)=18 on the K4-free order-18 graph; alpha is additive over components of A-S.

Component ceilings: alpha=1 forces a clique of order at most 3 (K4-free); alpha=2 forbids both I3 and K4, so order at most 8 by R(4,3)=R(3,4)=9, the same convention the accepted claim-connectivity-01 uses when it reads R(3,4)=9 as forcing K4 or I3. An alpha-3 component is K4/I4-free but otherwise unrestricted in order.

Total at most three is impossible: profiles (1,1),(1,2),(1,1,1) have orders at most 6,11,9, all below 18-t>=15. With total at most four, (1,1,2) caps at 14 and (1,1,1,1) at 12, both below 15, so alpha(A-S)=4 exactly and only (1,3) and (2,2) survive, each with exactly two components (the partition list into at least two parts is complete).
(2,2) arithmetic: both components are at most 8, so t=1 (order 17) is impossible, t=2 forces 8+8 (sum 16, each capped at 8), t=3 forces 7+8 in either order (sum 15).

Attachment bound (1,3): for z in S, N_C(z) has no triangle (triangle plus z is K4 in A) and no I4 (alpha(C)=3), so at most 8 vertices by R(3,4)=9; neighbors of z inside K_m are at most min(m,2) (three clique neighbors plus z would be K4). Edge classes of A are disjoint: clique internal C(m,2), C internal bounded by U(18-t-m), S-C attachments at most 8t, S-K_m attachments at most t*min(m,2), S internal at most C(t,2); K_m and C share no edges because they are distinct components of A-S. Replayed all nine substitutions against the census rows U(12)=40, U(13)=45, U(14)=50, U(15)=55, U(16)=60, U(17)=68: 69,66,63 / 74,72,69 / 80,79,76 all match.

(2,2) ceilings: a component vertex's neighborhood inside its own component is triangle-free (else K4) and I3-free (component alpha=2), hence at most 5 by R(3,3)=6, giving e<=floor(5n/2): 20 at n=8, 17 at n=7; each S vertex has at most 5 neighbors per component, 10 total; e(S)<=C(t,2). Totals 20+20+20+1=61 and 17+20+30+3=70 match, and the claim correctly labels them elementary, not sharp.

Case coverage and quantifiers are complete and correctly scoped to pure A with t in 1,2,3 and no q,E,x restriction; the proof does not reuse the order-18 disconnected classification for order-17/16/15 components, as the ledger promises.

Dependency applicability first: claim-connectivity-02 is stated for ambient G[A], and this claim's scope is pure. Its proof consumes only alpha=4 (heredity plus R(4,4)), the (1,3) profile partition, and the census maxima U(15)=55, U(16)=60, U(17)=68, all pure-graph facts, so a<=68 for disconnected pure A follows; equivalently it is claim 1's method run at t=0. The cited dependency applies without importing any ambient hypothesis.

Threshold direction: separator caps are one-directional (separator of size s exists implies a<=cap_s), and the proof uses the contrapositive correctly. Maxima by cut order: 68 (disconnected), 69 (t=1; the (2,2) branch is impossible there), 74 (t=2; max of 74,72,69,61), 80 (t=3; max of 80,79,76,70). Thus a>=70 excludes all cuts of order at most 1 (kappa>=2), a>=75 excludes order at most 2 (kappa>=3), a>=81 excludes order at most 3 (kappa>=4). Translations a=85-q give q<=15, q<=10, q<=4 exactly.

k(q) is total on integer q>=0 with bands (<=4, 5..10, 11..15, >=16); each of the first three bands maps to an established threshold, and the last band uses only kappa>=1 from explicitly assumed connectedness. The scope flags the connected hypothesis where it is needed.

Minimum-degree step: if d_A(u)=s<k(q)<=4, deleting N_A(u) leaves u isolated together with 18-1-s>=14 other vertices, a separator of size s<k(q), contradicting kappa>=k(q); at k(q)=1 connectedness alone forbids s=0. The claim does not assert sharpness, and the leaf witnesses at a=69,62 (q=16,23) are consistent because they sit in the k(q)=1 band.

(1,3) profile: fix u in K_m omitted by the actual column C_y and an independent triple T in C disjoint from C_y. The five vertices {u} union T union {y} are mutually nonadjacent: u is anticomplete to C because they lie in different components of A-S, y misses u and T by choice, T is independent. That is an I5 in G, forbidden. Hence C minus C_y contains no independent triple and is K4-free, so has order at most 8 by R(4,3)=9, giving |C_y intersect C| >= 18-t-m-8 = 10-t-m. Scalars 10-t-m give (8,7,6), (7,6,5), (6,5,4), all matching. The proof correctly needs neither I4-freeness of A nor any incidence on S, and the conclusion is stated as a dichotomy: K_m subset C_y, or the floor.

(2,2) profile: if both X minus C_y and Y minus C_y contained independent pairs, those four vertices form an I4 in A (no edges between distinct components of A-S) missed by the column, so {I4, y} is I5 in G, forbidden. Therefore one remainder is I3-free, hence a clique, hence of size at most 3 by K4-freeness (empty set included), giving |C_y intersect X|>=|X|-3 or |C_y intersect Y|>=|Y|-3. Component orders 8,8 yield a column of size at least 5; orders 7,8 yield at least 4.

The scalar floors are correctly scoped to the (2,2) bullet: a (1,3) column that contains a clique vertex need not reach 5, and the claim does not say so. All conclusions are necessary conditions on genuine columns of actual candidates, not existence assertions.

Row floors combine correctly for the stated connected-A scope: d_A>=k(q) from the accepted connectivity thresholds, d_A>=L=max(0,6-q) from the E(4,5,17)=79 deletion floor, d_A>=epsilon_u from the mixed-cell floor, giving d_A>=max(F,epsilon_u). With the independent cap r_u<=17 (reductions 5.2) and the exact identity r_u=17+epsilon_u-d_A(u), both r_u<=17 and r_u<=17+epsilon_u-F hold, i.e. r_u<=min(17,17+epsilon_u-F). For excess-zero rows r_u<=17-F; if only connectedness is invoked (min degree 1) while L=0, then F>=1 and r_u<=16, exactly the stated improvement over the old 17.

Pointed average: 2a=170-2q. Every excess-i neighbor (i=1..6, the full positive-excess range since 0<=epsilon<=6 in pivot section 1) has internal degree at least max(F,i) because both floors apply to it. The t=m_0 remaining internal degrees therefore sum to at most 170-2q-sum_{i}m_i*max(F,i), so one of them is at most the floor of that average. Membership in m_0 fixes global degree 18, and N(v)=A exactly, so for that neighbor lambda_vu=|N(v) intersect N(u)|=d_A(u). The cap 13 is the recorded edge-codegree cap of reductions 4.3 (the (3,5) cell), and the same averaged vertex satisfies lambda_vu>=F from its own floor, so the two-sided statement about one vertex carries no conjunction problem.

Example profile replay: q=15, m_0=10, m_1=8, all other m_i=0 gives 2a=140, E=8, x=136+30+8=174. Old floors contribute 8*max(0,-9,1)=8, so min(13,floor(132/10))=13; new floors contribute 8*max(2,1)=16, so min(13,floor(124/10))=12; F=2 gives excess-zero rows r_u<=15. All four numbers match the claim, and feasibility is explicitly disclaimed.

Separator-profile inequalities: a K_m vertex has A-neighbors only in (K_m-u) union S, so d_A(u)=m-1+|N_A(u) intersect S| <= m-1+|S|, and epsilon_u<=d_A(u) follows from r_u<=17 via the identity. For u in K_m and w in C (nonadjacent, different components of A-S): their common A-neighbors lie exactly in S, counted by h; the vertex set partitions as {v} union A union B; v is a common neighbor. So global codegree is exactly 1+h+|R_u intersect R_w|. The nonedge band [1+max(epsilon_u,epsilon_w), 8+epsilon_u+epsilon_w] from reductions 4.3 rearranges to both asserted inequalities, with the lower one clamped at 0.

Dependency hygiene: the claim cites P-pivot sections 1,2 for the excess range and floors and P-interface for the codegree bands and row cap; the concurrent interior_transfer.json is explicitly not used as a premise, as its concrete_prior_improvement states.

Universal-root conclusions: pivot section 3 gives q<=4+W/2 for EVERY degree-18 root (from q+E<=W/2+4 and E>=0), with no selection involved. W=0 gives q<=4, a>=81, kappa>=4; W<=10 gives q<=9, a>=76>=75, kappa>=3. Because the bound is universal it legitimately applies to both endpoints of any guaranteed adjacent pair, including companions of arbitrarily chosen roots.

Selected-root conclusions: pairwise-04's table, read in full, gives q_*<=4 at the maximum-edge root for W=0,2,4,6 and q_*<=5 for W=8,10, with the verbatim statement that the SAME selected root satisfies the bound and pointed-pair table. q<=4 gives a>=81 and kappa>=4; q<=5 gives a>=80, which supports only kappa>=3, and the claim correctly stops there. The scope restricts this bullet to explicitly selected roots, respecting cliques_augmentation section 3 (safe for existence coverage, not imposable on an arbitrary fixed root).

Companion conclusions: existence is guaranteed at W<=10 by pivot section 3 (each root has a degree-18 neighbor, E_v<=W<18) and by pairwise-04 (E_v<=10<18) for the selected root. The companion's connectivity uses only the universal q bound; the proof states explicitly that the companion's q need not equal the selected root's and that no independently chosen family pair is identified with this pair. I checked for an unsupported conjunction: every property attributed to one pair is either universal (connectivity of both endpoints) or taken from pairwise-04's own pointed pair (overlap caps), so none is cross-attributed.

W-table cross-check: pivot section 3's W-table (neighborhood edges 81..85, 80..85, 79..85, 78..85, 77..85, 76..85; overlap column 9,9,10,11,12,12) and pairwise-04's table (q_* 4,4,4,4,5,5; x_* 144,145,146,147,149,150; overlap 9,9,10,11,12,12) both reproduce the numbers the claim calls unchanged. The x caps independently re-derive as 136+q_*+(W/2+4) from q+E<=W/2+4 and x=136+2q+E: 144,145,146,147,149,150. No new caps and no strengthening are claimed, consistent with the wording.

claim_outcomes.reason_for_changes_requested: Dependency metadata defect only (finding F2): conclusions 2 and 4 rely on this file's claim-connected-density-connectivity, but the dependencies array lists only P-ramsey, P-interface, P-pivot. Repair: add claim-connected-density-connectivity to the dependencies array. The mathematical content of all four conclusions was independently verified and is correct.
independent_reasoning: Witness 1 (62 edges): an order-16 (4,4)-free H has alpha<=3 and is connected, because a disconnected H would have components under profiles with total alpha<=3, orders at most 6, 11, or 9, all below 16. The census rows (4,4,16): 60 min and 60 max mean EVERY such H has exactly 60 edges, so from any order-16 (4,4) graph attaching c-z-u with edges cz and zu yields exactly 62 edges. Any K4 would lie in H (new vertices have degrees 2 and 1); an independent set uses at most one of z,u (they are adjacent) so alpha<=1+alpha(H)<=4; the graph is connected and u is a leaf. Hence connected (4,5,18) implies neither d_A>=2 nor e>=69.

Witness 2 (69 edges): order-17 (4,4)-free H has exactly 68 edges (rows 68,68) and is connected by the same partition argument. Attach a leaf u to a fixed z: 69 edges, K4-free, alpha<=4. Deleting z isolates u while H-z retains 16 vertices, so z is a cut vertex: a connected (4,5,18) graph at a=69 with kappa=1, proving the threshold a>=70 cannot be lowered under the pure hypotheses. Every I4 contains u because H is I4-free; such an I4 exists because H-z on 16 vertices is K4-free and R(4,3)=9 supplies an I3, which extends by u (u's only neighbor is z, removed). So {u} is a genuine singleton transversal, tau=1: no column-size at least two conclusion can flow from connectedness through transversal size. The claim correctly frames this as a failure of that reasoning route rather than an ambient impossibility.

Ambient separation: the scope witness_limit and the conclusions both deny candidate or certified-neighborhood status. For a hypothetical leaf in an actual A, the identity r_u=16+epsilon_u together with r_u<=17 forces epsilon_u in {0,1}; the edge-codegree floor max(d(v),d(u))-18 equals epsilon_u and is satisfied at lambda_vu=1, so the floor alone indeed does not eliminate the leaf. The E=0 arithmetic x=136+2q (not q=0) matches c/w0's recorded failed route verbatim, as does the refusal to delete q>1 slices by connectedness; the q=1 theorem and the x136 closure are not imported. Because the witnesses sit at a=69 (q=16) and a=62 (q=23), the claim correctly bars using them to assert ambient realizability of those slices, and bars promoting the q=1 theorem to all connected A.

Defect recorded as F2: the kappa thresholds restated in conclusion 4 and the a>=70 threshold invoked in conclusion 2 are this file's claim-connected-density-connectivity; the proof itself says the separator conclusions continue to apply, but the dependencies field omits the claim link that sibling claims 2-5 all carry. Under the workflow dependency gates an unlisted edge would not propagate into pending review if the threshold claim changed, so the metadata must be repaired before acceptance.

findings.title: Claim 6 omits its dependency on claim-connected-density-connectivity
findings.body: Conclusion 2 of claim-connected-shortcut-obstructions asserts that the threshold a>=70 for two-connectivity cannot be lowered to 69, which presupposes the a>=70 threshold established by this file's claim-connected-density-connectivity, and conclusion 4 restates that claim's kappa thresholds (>=4 at q<=4, >=3 at q<=10, >=2 at q<=15) for the E=0 branch; the proof text itself chains to the separator conclusions. The dependencies array (line 170) lists only P-ramsey, P-interface, P-pivot, while sibling claims in the same file all list their intra-file claim links (claims 2, 3, 4, 5 each do). Impact: under the workflow gate that a changed or withdrawn dependency puts affected dependents into pending review, a future revision of claim-connected-density-connectivity would not flag this claim. The mathematics of all four conclusions verified correct; only the metadata entry is wrong.
